articles.title: XPeng Motors humanoid robot unit Dogotix raises $900M
articles.summary: XPeng Motors’ humanoid robotics subsidiary Dogotix raised more than $900 million in an initial funding round, valuing the business at more than $6.3 billion post-transaction. XPeng plans to use the capital for hardware and software development, data collection, physical AI model training, mass-production facilities, and global expansion, with a target of producing 1,000 IRON humanoids per month by the end of 2026 and starting commercial deliveries in 2027.

articles.title: XPENG IRON humanoid robot draws record physical AI funding
articles.summary: XPENG’s physical AI unit raised over $900 million at a $6.3 billion valuation to scale its IRON humanoid robot platform, which the company says is the largest single-round private capital raise in China’s physical AI industry to date. The funding, led by IDG Capital with participation from Tencent, Alibaba, and Gaorong Ventures, will support R&D, physical AI model training, data generation, mass production facilities, and overseas commercial expansion. XPENG expects IRON to enter mass production by the end of 2026, with customer deliveries in China and overseas markets planned for 2027.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is a concrete example of AI moving from software and cloud models into capital-intensive physical platforms, with implications for robotics supply chains, edge AI chips, manufacturing automation, and EV-adjacent technology ecosystems. The deal also highlights investor willingness to fund long-duration AI hardware commercialization despite pressure on XPENG’s core vehicle business and share price, creating a useful advisor discussion around both opportunity and execution risk in physical AI.

articles.title: NIST Researchers Supersize Quantum Technology to Help Detect Faint Photons

articles.title: Google Research Introduces ME-POIs: A Mobility-Informed Framework that Adds “How a Place Is Used” to Text-Based POI Embeddings
articles.summary: Google Research introduced ME-POIs, a framework that combines aggregate human movement data with text-based point-of-interest embeddings to capture not just what a place is, but how it is used. articles.title: HP1800: The Magic of Single-Stage 48V to Ultra-Low Voltage
